podcast.title: Mambo Craze of the 1950s
podcast.body: Mambo was a significant musical trend that gained popularity in the pop markets during the 1950s, particularly around 1953-1954. Named after Perez Prado's song "Mambo Jambo," it was part of a broader category of "Exotica" music from various Latin American and Caribbean cultures, and for a period, it was considered a strong contender to shape the future of music alongside rock and roll. "This was a craze named after a song by the Cuban band leader Peres Prado, Mambow Jambow."
